step1_summary.Vital signs/exam findings: No measured temperature, patient denies fever

V: Urinary tract bleeding secondary to vascular malformation or bladder trauma - could cause hematuria and pain.
I: Urinary tract infection (UTI)/cystitis: Classic presentation with dysuria, hematuria, lower abdominal pain, unpleasant urine smell, no systemic symptoms yet.
Urethritis (e.g., from STI): Pain on urination and hematuria possible.
Acute cystitis with subclinical infection: localized inflammation causing symptoms without fever.
N: Bladder neoplasm: Hematuria and irritative voiding symptoms could suggest early tumor, less likely due to age and acute onset.
D: Urolithiasis (bladder or urethral stones): Pain on urination, hematuria, lower abdominal pain; no flank pain stated.
I2: Medication-induced cystitis: Mebeverine unlikely to cause cystitis; no recent new meds or toxins mentioned.
C: Congenital urinary tract abnormalities causing recurrent infections or hematuria - no prior history makes congenital less likely.
A: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome: chronic condition, less likely first presentation.
Allergic reaction causing cystitis - no new exposures noted.
T: Traumatic injury to urinary tract causing hematuria and pain - no history of trauma.
E: Endocrine causes (e.g., diabetes with urinary symptoms) - no mention of diabetic symptoms or history.
